classification.difficultyReason: Combine the two marked lengths to obtain the quadrant radius, recognise the unshaded region as a right triangle with legs of 4 cm, and subtract its area from the quadrant before rounding.

content.prompt: Find the shaded area to 2 d.p.

spec.description: A quadrant with its centre at the lower vertex and radial sides extending upwards left and right. Each radius has two segments labelled 4. A horizontal chord joins the radial midpoints. Only the region between this chord and the outer arc is shaded. External segmented dimension arrows, a central right-angle marker and the source measurement notes are retained.
spec.mathematics: The two radii have length 4 + 4 = 8 cm and enclose 90 degrees. The excluded central triangle has perpendicular legs of 4 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Question givens and shaded target region only; no supplied answer or solution annotations.

answer.worked:
The two semicircles removed from the ends have the area of one circle of radius $\frac{8}{2}=4$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}A_1&=16\times8\\A_1&=128\ \mathrm{cm}^2\\A_2&=\pi(4)^2\\A_2&=16\pi\ \mathrm{cm}^2\\A_{\text{Total}}&=A_1-A_2\\A_{\text{Total}}&=128-16\pi\\A_{\text{Total}}&\approx77.73\ \mathrm{cm}^2\end{align*}$$
